2
When a beam of light is incident on a surface, it delivers energy to the surface. The intensity of
the beam is defined as the energy delivered per unit area per unit time.
What is the unit of intensity, expressed in SI base units?
A
kg m–2
s–1
B
kg m2
s–3
C
kg s–2
D
kg s–3

hints: Start from the definition given: intensity = energy / (area x time), so its unit is $\text{J m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1}$.
Recall energy in SI base units from work $W = Fs$: joule = $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$.
Divide that energy unit by $\text{m}^2$ for per unit area, then by $\text{s}$ for per unit time, and cancel the powers of $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Write intensity from the definition as $intensity = energy/(area \times time)$, so unit = $\text{J m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1}$.
Express the joule in base units: from $W = Fs$, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$.

A.explanation: This has $\text{m}^{-2}$ left over, which would mean the $\text{m}^2$ from energy was divided twice by area.

B.explanation: This is the base-unit form of energy in joules, $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, before dividing by area and time.

C.explanation: This is energy divided by area only, $\text{kg s}^{-2}$, and misses the extra $\text{s}^{-1}$ for per unit time.

D.explanation: Energy $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{m}^2$ and by $\text{s}$ gives $\text{kg s}^{-3}$.
